content: If someone is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load measurements, and T-cell counts. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Nevirapine, sold under brand names such as Viramune XR, has been associated with rare but severe, and sometimes fatal, liver problems and skin/allergic reactions. Women are at a higher risk of developing these severe reactions. To reduce the risk of skin/allergic reactions, nevirapine is initiated at a lower dose for the first 14 days. Individuals with higher T-cell counts at the start of treatment are at greater risk for liver complications. It is crucial to keep all medical and laboratory appointments so your doctor can monitor your response to nevirapine. The risk of these serious side effects is highest during the first 18 weeks of treatment, particularly within the first 6 weeks. If you have discontinued nevirapine due to liver problems or skin/allergic reactions, you must never take any form of nevirapine again. Nevirapine is used in combination with other HIV medications to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves quality of life. However, nevirapine is not a cure for HIV. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Nevirapine is not intended for preventing HIV infection after accidental exposure, such as needle sticks or contact with blood or bodily fluids. Before starting nevirapine, read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets. If you have never taken nevirapine before, you must first take the immediate-release form for 14 days before transitioning to the extended-release form. If you have already taken the immediate-release form for more than 14 days, you may begin the extended-release tablets immediately. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you stop taking this medication for more than 7 days for reasons other than the serious reactions described in the warning section, consult your doctor for instructions on how to restart treatment. It is critical to take this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, increase your dose, take it more frequently than prescribed, or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s guidance. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects may include tiredness, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Rarely, drowsiness may occur. You may notice the empty extended-release tablet shell in your stool, which is normal. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. These reactions can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Nevirapine commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare, but seek immediate medical attention if it occurs. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking nevirapine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may rarely cause drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase drowsiness. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and nevirapine may be part of that treatment. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of nevirapine from your body, which may impact how nevirapine works. Examples include rifamycins (such as rifampin). Nevirapine can accelerate the removal of many other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Do not use prednisone to prevent a rash, as it can increase the risk of a rash during the first 6 weeks of nevirapine treatment. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222.
